taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 14.369 | 0.124 | 0.12415
2 | 15.965 | 8.25 | 9.665
3 | 4591.4 | 27.074 | 47.738
4 | 5101.5 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Ulakwo, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Station Ulakwo, Etche LGA**

The VES interpretation at Ulakwo reveals a four-layer subsurface sequence. Layer 1 is a thin topsoil/clay horizon (14.37 Ω·m, 0.12 m thick), overlain by Layer 2, a slightly more resistive sandy/clayey unit (15.97 Ω·m, 8.25 m thick, base at 9.67 m). Layer 3 is a highly resistive unit (4591.4 Ω·m, 27.07 m thick, base at 47.74 m), likely coarse sand or gravel, and Layer 4 is the resistive basal layer (5101.5 Ω·m), interpreted as the main aquifer or bedrock.

Resistivity increases progressively with depth (r1 < r2 < r3 < r4), consistent with a continuously ascending resistivity trend. Applying the curve-type rule to each three-layer group yields A (layers 1-2-3) and A (layers 2-3-4), giving AA, written as A. This matches the on-file classification.

{"curve_type_stated": "A", "label_issue_flagged": false}
